chunks: And in the narration of Jamīl ibn Darrāj:

Regarding a woman who marries during her waiting period ('iddah), he said: "They must be separated, and she must observe one waiting period from either of them. If she gives birth to a child after six months or more, then the child belongs to the latter husband; and if she gives birth to a child in less than six months, then the child belongs to the former husband."

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman under discussion in the legal ruling
key_terms.عِدَّتِهَا: her waiting period after a prior marriage
key_terms.وَلَدٍ: a child born from the disputed union
key_terms.يُفَرَّقُ: they are to be separated legally

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman marries during her 'iddah, and to which husband is the child attributed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a woman who marries while still in her 'iddah. It states that the couple must be separated, that she observes a single waiting period, and it establishes paternity based on whether the child is born before or after six months.
